Assign a direction only when a supplied rule supports it. Positive and negative predictions need not be
equally common; leave unresolved cases as No visible cue.

entity relationships. The marked token need not itself be a cue word, symbol or part of the expression.
Do not add or enforce that requirement. Spaces, punctuation and ordinary words can carry the contextual
pattern. Continuation
clarifies meaning but was not an input to the measured position.

cannot establish a direction. Use no-visible-cue with predicted_pole uncertain when no condition supports

Return every requested ID with group, predicted_pole and a brief reason naming the specific contextual

claim.title: Colorado named-entity/local-format detector with contrastive non-Colorado suppression
claim.lede: Positive activation is dominated by explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder places and institutions, especially when they occur in Colorado legal, governmental, educational, health, local-news, or contact contexts; the high value often appears on an adjacent space, punctuation mark, digit, or function word rather than on the cue token itself. Negative activation is weaker and less coherent, but it concentrates in non-Colorado state/agency/contact/citation formatting and other-state or foreign geographic/natural-heritage named entities.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would revise or abandon the Colorado-specific explanation if, after controlling for exact Colorado/Denver/Boulder named entities and Colorado institutional/citation contexts, many strong positive examples remain unexplained by those names while many non-Colorado contact/citation blocks become positive. The negative account would change if punctuation/digit form alone predicts negative activation across Colorado and non-Colorado contexts, or if many other-state/foreign geographic named entities without administrative/citation formatting cease to be negative. A finding that 'Colorado' itself does not predict high activation once local news/government/source type is controlled would also weaken the main hypothesis.
claim.one_paragraph: The strongest lexical pattern is an explicit Colorado place name: ' Colorado', 'Denver', 'Boulder', 'CU', 'Colo', 'oulder', and closely related city/institution names. Token selectivity is extreme for ' Colorado' (mean ~94), 'Denver' (~97), 'Colorado' (~99), 'Boulder' (~75), with hit fractions of ~0.82-0.90 above the high threshold. Matches: 88026454 ('Colorado became... nickname is the Centennial State'), 24912 ('University of Colorado Boulder'), 8343 ('Denver Museum'), 9562952 ('Longmont, CO'), 10748 ('in Colorado'), 71436260 ('in Colorado... Vail Valley of Colorado'). The marked token can be ' is', 'the', ' at', a space, comma, or digit adjacent to the cue. Similar cases that do not match well: generic 'Rocky Mountain', 'Springs', 'Pueblo', 'Aspen', 'Mesa' are weaker (hit fractions roughly 0.15-0.34) and usually need an explicit Colorado/Denver cue; generic Nevada, Alaska, or New Mexico-only geography often does not activate positively. Passages containing Colorado legal or administrative references produce very high positive values, often on citation numbers, spaces, or nearby function words: '§ 22-5-119, C.R.S.', '22-5-199, C.R.S.', 'state of Colorado recognizes...', 'county', 'Department of Education'. Strong examples: 58669764/58669797/58669917 have very high product on spaces, '9', and 'Colorado' around the Blended Learning statutory citation; 12155 ('county' ~87) and 68975890 ('at' 298) fit Colorado state-government contexts. This is not just any statute or phone/address format: non-Colorado statutory/contact formats such as N.D.C.C. § 28-33-02, North Dakota phone numbers, or Qinghai grant numbers are negative. The delimiter alone is insufficient; a preceding Colorado/state-government cue is needed. High positive responses recur around Colorado local media, contact blocks, tourism/recreation, and named institutions: 'Local stories from 9NEWS' (71837166), 'Steamboat Today' (51755), Denver/Boulder/CSU/University of Colorado/Colorado College/Colorado School of Public Health, .colostate.edu URLs, 303/720/970 phone numbers in Colorado contexts. Examples include 46499 ('Atmospheric Science at Colorado State University'), 89775 ('Colorado School of Public Health'), 54086 ('Colorado State University'), 9562952 ('Longmont, CO'), 3530404 ('.colostate.edu' URL). The high value may land on ' at', ' the', ' Science', ' Public', a space before a phone number, or a slash in a URL. A national news, generic education, or non-Colorado contact block without the Colorado/Denver/Boulder name is usually weak or negative. Colorado political and civic phrases often produce strong positive responses, especially when a local official, county, school district, or state label is present: 'Colorado has released an update of its state climate plan... Gov. John Hickenlooper announced' (68975890; ' at' 298), 'Colorado became the thirty-eighth state... Centennial State' (88026454; ' is' 286, 'the' 268), county commissioners/county structure (12155; ' county' 87), Colorado child-poverty/local-government reporting (26513; space 152). This subpattern is closely related to P1-P3 and likely shares the Colorado named-entity core. It should not be broadened to 'any politics': a non-Colorado Latin America article has a high ' president' outlier (4422, product 135), which is not explained by the Colorado pattern and suggests either polysemy/noise or a weaker state-government/political-title component.
claim.negative_pole: Many strong negative values occur in administrative contact or citation formatting for other states or agencies: North Dakota Department of Agriculture 'Phone: (701) 328-1504' (32442428; negatives on ':', '(', digits), North Dakota Game & Fish contact '701-328-6302' (42760175; space before phone -39.75), Elko, Nevada club phone numbers (13854828), N.D.C.C. § 28-33-02 (30837117; hyphen/digits near -40), and Qinghai grant numbers '(No. 2016-ZJ-...)' (73735612; '(', '.', digits). The marked token is often a delimiter or digit, but the prefix names a non-Colorado agency/contact/citation. This pattern fails for identical formats in Colorado contexts, which are positive (e.g. Colorado C.R.S./contact examples), and bare numbers without such context are near zero. Negative activation concentrates on non-Colorado geographic and natural-heritage named entities: 'Alaska Natural Heritage Program' (3819061; ' Natural' -38), 'Loktak Lake... North East India' (19148625; comma -38.5), Qinghai/Tibet/Xinjiang area wording before '278,400' (33203795; space -44.5), Nevada '13,063-foot Wheeler Peak' (76354659/76354612; commas/digits around -41 to -44). Negative token selectivity also flags Dakota, Alaska, Cascade, Tahoe, Moj, Wild, Tribal, etc. However, this is not 'any non-Colorado geography': many non-Colorado geographic passages are only weakly negative or near zero, and Colorado-adjacent names such as Rocky, Springs, Pueblo, or Aspen can be weak positive. Some high negatives land on personal or organizational proper names in non-Colorado local, ethnic, or cultural contexts: 'Kumar' in 'Prem Kumar, the President of Thang-Ta Federation of India' (38306945; -38), 'Natural' in Alaska Natural Heritage (3819061), and negative token statistics include 'Incorporated', 'Kumar', 'Cascade', 'Fargo', etc. This is a weaker secondary pattern, not a general name penalty: many named entities elsewhere have near-zero activation, and Colorado names are strongly positive. It may reflect a contrastive named-entity/local-source suppression rather than a stable personal-name feature. Negative peaks often sit on punctuation inside numeric strings: hyphens in '28-33-02', parentheses or commas around '278,400' or '13,063', phone-number digits, and grant codes. A purely syntactic explanation is possible: the neuron may suppress certain numeric-delimiter patterns when they occur outside the Colorado/admin context. This hypothesis is weakened because the same delimiters and numbers in Colorado statutory/contact contexts are positive, and many other bare numbers do not fire. It therefore needs the additional 'non-Colorado administrative/citation context' condition.

Pembina Band of Chippewa Indians
History[edit | edit source]
It is not known exactly how long the Pembina Chippewa's have lived from northwestern Minnesota, eastern North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, northwestern Ontario, southern Manitoba, and Saskatchewan. 19th century books and reports about the Pembina Chippewa's are helpful. Historians generally classify the Pembina Chippewa's as being Saulteaux Indians but history tells of a Pembina Chippewa District.
A letter written by Father Belcourt to Major Woods in 1849, described the district of these Chippewa people. Belcourt claimed from Pembina, North Dakota, the Pembina Chippewa District extended around 400 miles from north to south. Belcourt claimed it commenced at the 49th parallel of latitude or the border of Canada and the United States. Belcourt only included the Pembina District land in the United States. Pembina District in the United States, extended from just north of Pembina, North Dakota at the Canadian border, to extreme southeastern South Dakota adjacent to Iowa.
Belcourt also told Woods that the Pembina Chippewa District extended over 500 miles from east to west, at the height of land where the Mississippi River is in Minnesota. That be the 47th parallel of latitude (the Leech Lake Reservation region). That be from Cass Lake over 500 miles to the west. Probably just southeast of what is now Fort Peck Reservoir. The Pembina Chippewa District bordered theLittle Shell Band of Chippewa Indians, Montana District. These Districts had close ties with the Lake Superior ChippewaDistrict to their east. The Yellowstone River in Montana may have been the Districts border. To the west was the Little Shell Chippewa District and to the east was the Pembina Chippewa District. Pembina Chippewa land in Canada was located in northwestern Ontario, Manitoba, and probably a small area of southeastern Saskatchewan. In the early 20th century, many Pembina Chippewa's who lived in southern Manitoba (St. Peters near Selkirk) were forced to relocate to the north and northeast. That be the Fisher River and Peguis region of Manitoba, and the region east of Lake Winnipeg in Manitoba and northwestern Ontario. That happened when adhesion's were signed to Treaty 5 on August 24, 1908 (Fisher River) and June 9, 1910 (Deer's Lake). Long before that, however, the Pembina Chippewa's migrated north into northern Manitoba and Nunavut.
Historians think the Chippewa's became attracted to the plains in the 18th century. And the fur trade was not as important to the Chippewa's as historians suggest. When the Chippewa's had the opportunity to trade they often did. However, they were prone to keep away from the white trading posts for a good reason. Trading companies knew it and lured the Chippewa's to the trading posts by offering alcohol. Chippewa leaders found it extremely difficult to stop their subjects from visiting the trading posts and were probably forced to use harsh measures to keep them away from the trading posts. All too often it failed.
By the late 18th century, the Pembina Chippewa's were living in the Devil's Lake region of North Dakota and also the Turtle Mountains region of North Dakota and Manitoba. To the south of Devil's Lake, the Lakota, who had yet to be subjugated by the Pembina Chippewa's, used the guns they received from white trading posts to attack the Pembina Chippewa's. At the time the Chippewa soldiers could easily defeat the Lakota using only bows and arrows. The single shot musket guns were no match. Some Lakota people were always capable of not being subjugated by the Chippewa's. They tended to keep their villages located near white trading posts.
Some time in the 18th century, the Pembina Chippewa's had forced their way into the east of South Dakota. They mixed their culture and language with the Lakota people they had subjugated. It is not known when the Pembina Chippewa's reached the Montana region. According to the Chippewa author Peter Jones, the Chippewa's had fought a war in far western Montana (around the Missoula and Bitterroot Valley region) many generations before his time which was the mid 19th century. Jones could only provide those details.
Since Jones wrote the event occurred Many Generations before his time, that may indicate it was a period of more than 100 years. A few generations is maybe about 5. Many generations can actually add up to 10, 20 or even more. However, William W. Warren wrote that the Ojibway people counted one generation as being 40 years. So the Chippewa war in far western Montana, possibly occurred 200 to 400 to 800 years before Jones time which was the mid 19th century. That be anywhere between the 1000s, 1400's and 1600's. And Peter Jones was not the only author to write about the Chippeway's fighting a war in far western Montana.
Around the time of the War of 1812, the whites launched an invasion into the south of Manitoba. Pembina Chippeway soldiers defeated and subjugated them. They allowed the whites who had settled in the few white forts and settlements in southern Manitoba, some degree of freedom. Freedom of religion was one and to stay in contact with the whites at the trading posts was another. The Metis people are a part of Pembina Chippewa history.
They liked the lifestyle of the Pembina Chippewa's who frequently hunted for buffalo. They are a mixture of Chippewa and white, or the descendants of the white settlers who invaded southern Manitoba between 1800 and 1820. They would cause problems as the 19th century progressed. The Pembina Chippewa's mixed their culture and language with the whites they subjugated. Much mixing occurred and the Metis were prone to fall for the religion of the whites. The Pembina Chippewa's were liberal about religion but were not stupid. They first allowed the whites to carry on with their religion but sometimes reacted with great rage if the whites appeared to be foolish.
Brief Timeline[edit | edit source]
Were probably living in the south of Manitoba and northwestern Ontario. A larger Lake Winnipeg probably existed during those times so the Pembina Chippewa's were probably more at home in northwestern Ontario.
May have had first contact with the whites.
They definitely had contact with the whites. Probably from the Hudson Bay region. Pembina Chippeway soldiers were sent east to help fight the whites and their Indian allies.
Though their participation in the wars against the whites was limited, Pembina Chippeway soldiers did participate in those wars. In 1774 (around the time of Lord Dunmore's War or Revolutionary War), the whites commenced to build trading posts inland from Hudson Bay. It agitated the Chippeway's. After the Revolutionary War, an increase in the number of inland trading posts followed. Hudson Bay Company was really searching for the Northwest Passage. After finding it, they commenced to build forts in northern Alberta and the Northwest Territories. It caused unrest among the Chippeway's.
During the War of 1812, the whites launched an invasion to the south of Manitoba. Chippeway soldiers stopped and defeated the whites. They subjugated most until 1869. Wars on the plains of the northern United States and Minnesota, led to large numbers of Pembina Chippewa casualties. Many followed prophecy and fled west. Chief Yellow Quill, who originally lived in southern Manitoba, was instrumental in leading large numbers of Pembina Chippewa's to eastern Saskatchewan. One of chief Yellow Quill's sub-chiefs named Kinistin, led large numbers of Pembina Chippewa's north to the Barren Lands (Caribou Land) of Manitoba, northeastern Saskatchewan, and Nunavut. Chiefs James and John Smith, led large numbers of Pembina Chippewa's from the St. Peters region in southern Manitoba, to Saskatchewan. Many Pembina Chippewa's were led into Montana by chief Sitting Bull. Chief Sitting Bull was born and raised among the Red River Chippewa's, or was Pembina Chippewa.

Although it's a comedy, The Merchant of Venice is far darker than such sunny Shakespearean offerings as Much Ado About Nothing and A Midsummer Night's Dream. It's also a difficult piece for modern audiences because of the central figure of Shylock. Shylock is the money-lending Jew to whom Antonio, the merchant of the title, turns when he needs money. Antonio signs a "merry bond" -- which he believes to be a joke -- that states he will forfeit a pound of his own flesh if he cannot repay the debt. The money is given by Antonio to his friend, Bassanio, so that the latter can woo the rich, beautiful Portia, and the wooing goes well. But when Antonio's ships are lost at sea and he's unable to pay his debt, Shylock pursues the murderous penalty in the courts.
This plot is derived from anti-Semitic medieval sources. During the trial scene, Shylock seeks justice and revenge in Old Testament terms, and Portia asserts the primacy of mercy -- which she and the court see as a purely Christian attribute. Antonio comes within a hair's breadth of losing his life; the young Venetians cheer the Jew's ultimate humiliation. This scene is intensely uncomfortable to watch; it's hard to square it with the love entanglements and the fairy-tale story of Portia's suitors that make up the rest of the play.
The trial scene is followed by much teasing and laughter among the lovers and a lyrical interlude between Jessica, Shylock's daughter, and the Christian, Lorenzo, with whom she had eloped earlier.
How is a modern director to deal with all of this? In Shakespeare's time, Shylock was played in a flaming red wig as a caricature to be mocked and hated. In the nineteenth century, actors began focusing more on the character's humanity. "I look upon the role as the type of a persecuted race; almost the only gentleman in the play, and most ill-used," said the famed English actor Henry Irving.
It helped that Shakespeare, being Shakespeare, was unable to create an entirely two-dimensional character and had given Shylock a couple of extraordinary speeches, one revealing the daily humiliations he suffered and a second in which he passionately asserted his humanity: "I am a Jew. Hath not a Jew eyes? Hath not a Jew hands, organs, dimensions, senses, affections, passions?"
Some directors simply take out the most problematic language -- a slew of Christian jeers and such nasty Shylockian excesses as "I would my daughter were dead at my foot, and the jewels in her ear." Denver Center director Anthony Powell, however, has chosen to present The Merchant of Venice as written. It's a brave and intelligent choice, but also a risky one. If we acknowledge, as I think we have to, that the derision shown toward Shylock by the other characters would have been shared by Shakespeare and most of his contemporaries, that these people would have seen the forced conversion of a Jew as an unmitigated good, then the questions arise: Does the play still have value? How do we balance its anti-Semitism against its eloquence and charm? Are we to take Merchant as a historical document, justify it because no writer can see beyond the ethos of his own times, and decide that its poetry redeems what's ugly in it? I have no answers. Every time I see The Merchant of Venice, it leaves me more uneasy -- though I did attend a successful production in London in which the play became pure tragedy, with Shylock looming above the action, a figure as evil as Macbeth and as deeply wronged as Lear.
Material this tricky requires a strong directorial vision, and the Denver

Phlebotomy Career Guide
The practice of phlebotomy can be traced back to around 2000 years back. This was a common practice adopted by doctors till as late as the 19th century and was popularly termed as bloodletting previously. In many ancient civilizations such as the Greeks, Egyptians, Mesopotamians, Mayas and Aztecs, medical practitioners routinely used this process to treat people of different diseases. Hippocrates, who is acknowledged as the Father of Modern Medicine, used to prescribe bloodletting as an effective treatment for restoring sick people to health. But, it is Galen, one of his disciples, who’s thought to have introduced bloodletting as an innovative medical procedure.
Practitioners of modern medicine have largely discarded the age old practice of what was earlier referred to as phlebotomy although the term itself has been retained. Today, phlebotomy denotes the extraction of blood in the vein, artery or capillary of a patient and collecting it into test tubes for later analysis in labs or for using it for blood transfusion. Blood samples are collected from patients for treating or diagnosing different diseases.
The term phlebotomy has Greek origins. The word comes from the Greek roots”phlebo” which means”vein”,”tom” which means”to puncture” and”y” meaning”process”. The literal meaning of the term phlebotomy is consequently”the practice of puncturing veins”. And consequently, any medical professional who has been trained in withdrawing blood for subsequent testing or for the purpose of blood transfusion is referred to as a phlebotomist.
Overview of Phlebotomy Education
If you are interested in practicing phlebotomy in Las Vegas, you will need to undergo proper training in the various procedures involved as this field has strict health policies. Besides, the phlebotomy certification you obtain after receiving the necessary training would also make it easier for you to find employment.
There are many schools that offer training in phlebotomy today by way of on campus courses or online programs or a mix of both. So check them out and pick the phlebotomy training program of your choice. During training, you will learn how to draw blood properly without causing any pain to the patient, as well as how to prepare the blood sample for laboratory testing, how to handle it carefully and prevent it from getting infected. You’ll also learn how to put the patient at ease as you describe the medical procedure to him. In addition, phlebotomists are given specialized training in gathering the information doctors need for diagnosing a patient’s disease accurately.
Phlebotomy has a special significance in the modern healthcare industry where it is generally practiced by physicians, nurses and other professionals with the necessary training and qualifications such as phlebotomists. Nowadays, though collecting blood samples is vital for diagnosis and treatment of a range of ailments, doctors often find it hard to manage drawing blood out of increasingly large numbers of patients. Phlebotomists play an essential role in relieving the burden on doctors. Not surprisingly therefore, more and more hospitals and healthcare centers use the services of full-time phlebotomists.
Phlebotomy Training – First step to become a phlebotomist in Las Vegas Nevada
Are you interested in pursuing a career in the medical field? Are you looking for a healthcare job that requires minimal educational qualifications and the completion of a short training course? If it describes the job you’re searching for, then phlebotomy training are the best option for you. It can prepare you for a career as a phlebotomist.
Employment opportunities in Las Vegas are excellent for phlebotomists even in a slow market. Today, phlebotomy accounts for one of the most rapidly growing job sectors in the health care field. What’s most attractive about phlebotomist jobs is they come with above average salaries, are in high demand and require minimum time and education price. It is not unusual to find other medical professionals such as nurses and physicians paying for their medical school fees using their earnings from phlebotomist jobs. One that you choose to embark on a career as a phlebotomist, have a look at the phlebotomy training courses offered by phlebotomy schools in your state.
Phlebotomy plays an essential role in healthcare and needs special skills and expertise. You can acquire these by completing an approved training course and you can apply for phlebotomy certification, thus paving the way to a well paying job as a certified phlebotomist.
Phlebotomy is a specialized field in health care that requires the drawing of blood samples from people. Sterilized medical needles are used for this function and medical technicians who are trained and certified to carry out this procedure are called phlebotomists. If the blood sample is taken from a patient that requires medical treatment, it’s then analyzed and subjected to certain tests that will be carried out in a medical laboratory by trained technicians. The test results when assessed by a physician will give a clear picture of the patient’s illness and the line of treatment required.
A phlebotomy training course is of a relatively short duration, usually only around 15 weeks. In less than four months therefore you might be ready for your first job as a phlebotomist. Some phlebotomist training classes require candidates to complete at least 200 working hours within a clinical locale. During the training course you will learn how to collect blood without causing pain to patients, the way to handle it correctly and keep it secure for additional analysis. You will also learn various ways and techniques for performing venipuncture on patients.
Undergoing phlebotomy training from an accredited phlebotomy school is the first step in becoming a phlebotomist. The next step would be to get certified, then you can anticipate well paying employment as a certified phlebotomist.
How to become a Certified Phlebotomist in Las Vegas
With the advancement in medical sciences, plenty of career choices are being carved. One such area is Phlebotomy and is increasingly being taken up by kids who want to take up a job fast and at the same time need a satisfying career. If you are wondering about how to become a certified phlebotomist, this report may help you.
Phlebotomy is the process of withdrawing blood from the patients and is definitely a specialized field. The practice of withdrawing blood may seem easy but it requires plenty of skill, dedication and training. Many of the doctors and nurses in Nevada are not comfortable withdrawing blood from the patients as they might have specialized training in surgical procedures and nursing duties respectively. As the doctors and nurses are pre-occupied with their retinue duties, you need specialized people for withdrawing blood. This is one of the primary reasons as to why the Phlebotomists or Phlemotomy Technicians are in good demand. Phlebotomists are suitably placed and employed at all clinics, nursing homes, medical facilities, physician’s offices and all hospitals.
Undergoing Phlebotomy Training
Now, you need to understand how to be a Phlebotomist. First of all, you need to undergo a basic phlebotomy training course. The training course may vary from a few weeks to a month or two. The Phlebotomy training is a comprehensive training that includes both the classroom and practical sessions. You receive quality hands on training on all the facets of Phlebotomy. You’ll be trained under teachers who operate as phlebotomists themselves.
The phlebotomy training course will cover all aspects of how to utilize medical needles and medical equipment related to withdrawing blood. You want to clearly understand that the job of a Phlebotomist is quite important as a blood test needs to be completed for detecting any type of disease. There are loads of schools and institutes imparting quality Phlebotomy training. Before enrolling into any training course, you need to see the training institute and discuss about the course contents.
Getting Phlebotomy Certification
In order to take a certification test in Phlebotomy, you need to have completed a training course in Phlebotomy successfully and should have worked in a clinic, medical center or hospital for the specified time as required by the certification rules. As soon as you clear your certification tests, you become a certified phlebotomist who’s eligible for some high paying jobs. You would be happy to note that certified phlebotomists are being paid very well and it has now become a most sought after career.
Phlebotomy Certification Exam Questions in Nevada
So you want to make a career in phlebotomy and you are interested in knowing more about the phlebotomy certification exam.
Well, this article has just what you need for it answers most of the frequently asked questions about becoming a certified phlebotomist.
To begin with, ASCP is the contracted form of American Society for Clinical Pathologists Which will be the official licensing body which issues the phlebotomy technician certification to those who pass the certification exam.
Those who seek phlebotomy certification from ASCP fall into two broad categories:
1) those who have completed an approved training course and picked up The special techniques for drawing blood and performing other laboratory procedures; and
2) those who have obtained training on-the-job, and have experience of working in the phlebotomy field.
Passing the phlebotomy certification examination calls for prior preparation. The ideal way would be to receive a study guide, get familiar with the kinds of questions usually contained in the certification exam, and then try an adequate number of practice tests.

As you already know, the basic duty of a Phlebotomist would be to draw blood from the patients. The medical term for withdrawing blood from the individual is known as venipuncture. The phlebotomists are also required to adhere to proper blood collection methods. The blood withdrawn from the patients has to be stored properly in the bottles and the phlebotomists will need to label the health blood bottles properly. Under the oversight of the phlebotomists, the medical bottles are delivered directly to the suitable medical labs for tests to be carried out on the blood samples. Apart from these, the phlebotomists also perform many other important duties.
Besides physicians and nurses, even the phlebotomists are expected to exhibit excellent bedside manners and ought to be very kind to patients. Tons of times many patients could express fear and distress on the very thought of blood being withdrawn from their veins. It is during these times that the phlebotomists will need to speak soothing words and calm them down.
